newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras floods strand thousands, diseases feared.
newsitem.headline: Honduras floods strand thousands, diseases feared.

text.p: Rainstorms and heavy flooding killed 10 and left thousands stranded in northern Honduras on Monday as the country braced for feared epidemics of cholera, malaria and other diseases.

"The greatest problem and the risk that people face is in the stagnant waters, and the fact that there are still areas cut off where it is difficult to send in food," said Rosario Cabanas, head of the national hospital system.

She said in sweltering, dirt-poor northern towns like La Lima, stagnant waters were providing breeding grounds for malaria- and dengue-spreading mosquitos. Respiratory ailments, diarrhoea, skin fungi and lice were on the rise, she added.
Officials said two people died of cholera and another 10 cases were detected as drinking-water systems were destroyed in the disaster.
Ten days of lashing rain turned parts of the country into a virtual swamp, destroying brick houses as well as riverside shacks and coffee and banana crops.

On Monday helicopters were flying food to some isolated communities and residents began to shovel mud and debris from their homes, hoping to move back in. Other homeless stood by the sides of main roads waiting for pumps to clear the way back to their villages, said Rodil Henriquez, spokesman for the Permanent Contingency Committee.
At its peak the flooding drove more than 63,000 people from their homes and caused some $31 million in damage to crops, highways and bridges.
Japan has offered $100,000 to help the victims and Costa Rica has said it would provide $79,000 in medicines.
